Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Blue Harbor is seriously evaluating Redwood for our core inference tier. We're moving fast on budgeting and procurement and want to understand if you can accommodate a multi-year prepay with more flexible annualization. Specifically: 

- We'd like a 3-year commercial commitment but with the ability to annualize payments (yearly billing) and a modest usage-based true-up at the end of each year.

Hi Jared — thanks for the clear ask and for the forecast. Really appreciate the timeline.

High level we can do two alternative structures that map to what you're asking. Attached is a short proposal + term sheet (two options). Summary below: 

Option A — 3-year locked prepay (highest discount):
- Payment: Upfront prepay for 36 months
- Discount: 20% off standard list for committed units
- Ramp: Year 1 allocation = 60% of committed units, Year 2 = 85%, Year 3 = 100%
- Clawback: Not available for this option (tradeoff for deeper discount)

Option B — Annualized 3-year commitment with limited clawback (flexible):
- Payment: Annual billing (each year billed at the start of the contract year) for a 36-month term
- Effective discount: 14% base term discount, plus a variable uplift for multi-year billing cadence
- Ramp schedule: Year 1 = 55% of committed units, Year 2 = 80%, Year 3 = 100%
- Clawback mechanics: If actual usage in a contract year is >= 80% of that year's allocated commitment, no clawback. If usage < 80%, Blue Harbor receives a prorated credit equal to 50% of the unused prepaid capacity value for that year, applied as a credit to the next annual invoice or as a refund at year-end on request. Cap: clawback credits cannot exceed 10% of the annual prepaid amount.
- True-up: End-of-year reconciliation within 30 days; usage data and auditing hooks provided via the Redwood Console export.

Conditional requests we've included:
- If you require a clawback >10% cap, we would need an additional ~2–3% discount giveback (subject to approval).
- All annualized agreements require a signed amendment with the agreed ramp and clawback terms.

I've attached: BlueHarbor_Redwood_Proposal_v1.pdf and a short clawback-term-sheet.docx that spells the credit math.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which option you prefer (A or B) and any changes to the ramp breakpoints.
2) If Option B looks close, we'll route to finance and legal for redline and get back to you with the DocuSign prepared version.

I copied Marissa, who will coordinate the commercial approval path on our side. If you want, we can also do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the term sheet.

Thanks — Sofia
